column2: The whole earth ripened crops without ploughing, grain grew without the plough; infants were well nourished by their mothers' milk, women well nourished by their husbands' care.

People were well nourished, well protected by kings; the bull was well nourished when joined with truth. While the people were thus given to dharma and devoted to Hari, and were protected by the king's son, time passed, a cause of happiness.
Free of disease, rich in prosperity, celebrating festivals for many years, the lord of the earth, greatly bewildered, was joined with happiness arising from Mohini's doings.

He knew neither day nor night, nor month, fortnight, nor year; deeply infatuated by the love-making of the daughter of Brahma, of auspicious behaviour. In union with Mohini the king's power in love grew greater; the more the king enjoyed, the more his virility increased, as the cool-rayed moon in the bright fortnights is not diminished by constant service.
As a god renewed again and again by drinking the nectar, he touched and touched again, drinking sweet drink and hearing songs with fine words,
seeing the form of the fair-hipped women, touching Mohini's moon-like face again and again, pressing with his hand her high, full breasts resting on flesh,
her thick breasts like golden pots covered by necklaces, the three folds not overgrown, charming, with a line of fine hair,
looking all around at the beauty of her breasts he held the fair-eyed one: there was nothing more beautiful in the minds of fair-hipped women.
Whatever form was made by the Creator for Mohini's bewilderment: shanks like the paws of the lion-enemy (elephant), hairless, bright as molten gold,
a row of teeth with the lustre of the moon, hidden ankles for bewildering people — from foot to head that form, he saw, of the lovely wide-eyed one.
The king thought himself greater than the gods, greatly fulfilled with joy: "Ah, this slender, wide-eyed one — whatever she asks, that shall be given.
In her lovely union, at the end, I shall give her all my wealth; the hardly obtainable gift and what others cannot give — I shall give even what is not to be given to her.
Even my life, though not to be given, if the gold-hued one asks for it, I shall give it without hesitation. Except my son, nothing is ungiveable to her."

I brought ten thousand nagas' daughters, and from there also very many necklaces and jewels.
naradapuran:144:15	Again, father, I went to the great city of the demons and, having conquered them, brought away
naradapuran:144:16	three thousand five hundred beautiful, radiant girls and ten crores of jewels, for lamp-offerings on the approach of night.
naradapuran:144:17	They were brought to your palace, O king, as lamp-makers. Then I went to Varuna's world, standing at the bottom of the nether region,
naradapuran:144:18	proud of my valour and strength, a servant of your pair of feet. There I said to the god Varuna: 'Stay under my father's control,
naradapuran:144:19	if you wish to live, of King Rukmangada.' Angered at my words Varuna came to fight.
naradapuran:144:20	A terrible battle of a year took place in the nether world; I conquered that lord of waters with the Narayana weapon.
naradapuran:144:21	He was not killed, through the women's words to protect his life; being defeated, he gave ten thousand horses of the wind's speed,
naradapuran:144:22	on one side black-eared, white, moon-bright, which live many years without grass or water,
naradapuran:144:23	and in front of them a beautiful girl well adorned, Varuna gave for my wife, and that fair one was brought by me.
naradapuran:144:24	Maidens with great wealth were brought; there is no place in the three worlds, father, hard to reach
naradapuran:144:25	that I have not conquered by serving your feet. So rise, examine the prosperity earned by your grace.
naradapuran:144:26	And all these riches, O lord of men, are subject to you; a son who says, father, 'prosperity was earned by me'
naradapuran:144:27	and does not give it to Brahmins also goes to hell. A son should not boast of himself, father.
naradapuran:144:28	A son is like an axe and sickle in heaping up property; by the father's valour the son's heap of wealth increases.
naradapuran:144:29	Taking a shining sickle one cuts heaps of grass; a cloth filled with wind carries a boat across the water.
naradapuran:144:30	As a wooden doll moves by a juggler's will, so sons gain energy and strength by their father's vigour.
naradapuran:144:31	Therefore this one, beloved of Madhava (Hari?) and the gods, whom I have brought, look at her today; let the best of the companies of mothers, by her own will, give or protect her riches.
He punished the wicked and protected the good; he wandered in all countries and inspected all affairs.
Everywhere month by month he inspected the tasks; he maintained elephants and horses and saw to the spies' circle.
He inspected disputes, the scales and measures day by day, and the king protected each household of men.
Nowhere did a nursing child cry for lack of the breast; nowhere did a mother-in-law cry, insulted by her daughter-in-law.
Nowhere did a capable son ask his father (for money); none had mixture of classes in the kingdom.
People with hidden wealth did not speak ill of dharma; no wife with a husband was without a bodice.

Let women not go out of the house in my kingdom; let no widow have hair, nor a woman without a husband be without hair;
naradapuran:145:34	let no vow-keeper be always abusive; let none live as a forest-dweller in a city; the cruel who gives nothing at all of the common livelihood — let him not live in my kingdom.
naradapuran:145:35	The cowherd seeking the city, the useless preacher, or a priest without the scriptures — let him not live here in my kingdom.
naradapuran:145:36	One who makes indigo and one who sprinkles indigo dye — those two sinners are to be banished, as is one who makes liquor.
naradapuran:145:37	One who eats meat in vain, one fond of back-meat, has no residence in my kingdom, nor he who abandons his own wife.
naradapuran:145:38	Whoever, abandoning Vishnu, the best of the gods, worships any other god, or goes to a pregnant or newly delivered young woman, is to be punished and slain by us.

Now I wish to say it; understand, fair-faced one. Many Kartikas have passed while I was attached to you, goddess.
naradapuran:146:30	A man born in Kartika is not a vow-keeper except for Hari's day. I do not wish to spend Kartika without the vow.
naradapuran:146:31	For those mortals whose Kartika passes without a vow, their sacrifices and good works are in vain, and their dharma, since the Creator's birth.
naradapuran:146:32	Even kings who ate meat and were excessively fond of hunting gave up meat in Kartika and went to Vishnu's abode, auspicious one.
naradapuran:146:33	When a restriction is made in Kartika on foods one is used to, the practitioner surely attains Vishnu's form.
naradapuran:146:34	Let gifts of much wealth stay aside, fair one — the lamp-gift, which causes no heart-strain, takes one to heaven.
naradapuran:146:35	In absence of that, fair one, rousing another's lamp with devotion should be done, greater than all gifts.
naradapuran:146:36	On one side all gifts, on the other the lamp-gift; the awakening of the lamp is said to equal Kartika.
naradapuran:146:37	It should be done with devotion, said to be greater than all gifts. Having observed the Kartika tithi at the lotus of Vishnu's navel,
naradapuran:146:38	he is freed from sin done since birth, without doubt. One whose Kartika passes with vows, fasts and restraints
naradapuran:146:39	becomes a god in an aerial car and goes to the highest goal. Therefore, Mohini, give up your delusion about me,
naradapuran:146:40	and give your command at that time; I shall do the Kartika vow. I shall refrain from worshipping your breasts, lotus-eyed one,
naradapuran:146:41	and I shall become a vow-keeper in the worship of Hari. Mohini said: "Tell me in detail the greatness of Kartika.
This month is called the mine of all merit, O best of kings; where specially is it taught? Tell me, O great-minded one.
Having heard the greatness of Kartika I shall do as I wish."
Rukmangada said: "I shall tell the greatness of this month, fair-faced one, by which devotion to worship Hari will arise in you.
One who in Kartika practises Krichchhra or the Prajapatya, or fasts on alternate days, or fasts for three nights,
or ten days, a fortnight, or a month, fair one, having spent it, goes to Vishnu's supreme abode.
By eating once a day, eating at night, or not asking (for food), men obtain the earth with its garland of continents.
Especially at the holy place Pushkara, at Dvaravati and at Shukara, this month is declared to give devotion through vows, gifts, worship and so on.
On that, Hari's day is holy, and so is Bhishma-panchaka. A man who keeps the Prabodhini with a vigil
does not remain in a mother's womb, even if he is full of sin. On that day, fair-hipped one, whoever sees the circle,
without Sankhya or yoga goes to the highest state. Having seen the circle in Kartika, the boar of Shauri, auspicious one,
or the cow-boar, he is not born again as a son. By seeing it, men are freed from all three kinds of sin.
The circle, restless-eyed, Shridhara, and Kubja: in Kartika one should avoid oil; in Kartika one should avoid honey;
in Kartika avoid meat; in Kartika avoid women; in Kartika, goddess, one devoted to Vishnu should give up black-gram.
He is at once outside the sin done in a year; but from eating once he obtains a royal womb.
The fool who eats boar's meat in Kartika is cooked in Raurava for sixty thousand years.
Freed from that, the sinner is born a village-boar eating excrement. He should not eat fish, tortoise or deer meat.
By eating meat in Kartika, goddess, one is born a Chandala. Kartika destroys all sin for the one who keeps even a little vow.
Initiation done in Kartika cuts the birth of men; therefore with all effort one should take initiation in Kartika.
For the uninitiated, fair-thighed one, everything done is fruitless; a man without initiation obtains an animal's womb.
One should not keep Kartika at home, especially the Kartiki; a man keeping the Kartiki at a holy place goes to Hari's abode.
Having kept the Ekadashi of the bright half of Kartika, and given auspicious pots in the morning, a man goes to Hari's abode.
The completion of year-long vows is remembered as Kartika. Where weddings are seen at the lotus of Vishnu's navel (i.e., after Prabodhini),
four days there, as one, fair-hued one — even without the northern course or the purity of the ascendant,
where connections that increase sons and grandsons are seen. Therefore, Mohini, I shall do the Kartika vow-service
for the destruction of all sins and for increase of your pleasure." Mohini said: "Ah, incomparable greatness of Kartika, as told by you!
Tell the rule of conclusion of the Chaturmasya vows, by which the vows are made complete, O lord of the earth,
and the vow-fruit of merit is without defect." The king said: "One keeping the night vow should feed a Brahmin with six tastes, dear.
For not asking, he should give a bull with gold; one who abstains from meat should give a cow with a fee.
For bathing in the amalaka, a man should give curd and milk-rice; for restriction on fruits, fair-browed one, he should give fruit.
For giving up oil, he should give ghee; for giving up ghee, milk; for restriction on grains, rice or the grain itself.
For sleeping on the ground he should give a bed with mattress and pillow; the leaf-eater should give a vessel with ghee.
For silence, a bell or sesame with gold; the couple's meal should be done for both with a bed.
Intercourse with a fee for the completion of the vow; for bathing in the morning, a horse; for lack of oil, ghee and barley meal.
For wearing nails and hair, a mirror; for avoiding footwear, sandals should be given.
For giving up salt, a cow should be given; for abandoning meat, a tawny cow with her calf.
One who daily gives a lamp in a temple in the desired vow gives a gold or copper lamp with ghee, dear;
for completion of the vow he should give an umbrella with cloth to a Vaishnava. One fasting on alternate days should give silk.
For the three-night fast he should give a well-adorned bed with gold; for fasts of six nights and so on, a palanquin with an umbrella,
with a bearer and a stout draught-ox; for eating once, a goat or sheep; for living on fruit, gold;
for living on vegetables, he should give a golden fruit with ghee; for giving up all tastes, or the unnamed,
a silver vessel or a golden one as able should be given. If what is prescribed is not given or not done,
he should follow the words of Brahmins, fair-browed one, preceded by remembering Vishnu. Whoever thinks the Brahmin's words vain, auspicious one,
or does not give a fee, surely goes to hell; failing in the vow, he is born a leper and blind.
Who would transgress the words of the Brahmins, in whom stand the gods, holy places and sacrifices, fair-browed one — a wise man wishing for good?
This, joined with the secret of dharma, was told by me to Brahma as said by the Lord of Shri; it is revealed to you, to be told to none else, giving fruit and pleasing Madhava."

...a mortal is not a son, is not born in the womb again. Men, with your own wealth, practise worship of the discus-bearer.
naradapuran:147:40	With cloth, flowers, incense, lamps, best sandal, saffron, with friendly things, fruits and perfumes, worship Shri Hari's abode.
naradapuran:147:41	Whoever does not do my word today, which is righteous and gives the way to Vishnu, is to be punished and killed and surely banished from the realm.
While the drum, loud as a cloud, was being sounded thus, the best of kings, putting down the betel with camphor from his hand,
drew his heart that clung to Mohini's breasts and rose, the king, from the bed, increaser of love,
and said with soft speech to Mohini, tormented by delusion and desire: "Goddess, tomorrow will be Hari's day, destroyer of poverty.
I shall be restrained; forgive, forgive me. By your order I made Sandhyavali keep severe austerity.
This Ekadashi is to be kept by me, the one that awakens, cutter of the bond of all sin, giver of the goal,
maker of a great festival for all three worlds; therefore I shall eat havishya, restrained, O elephant-gaited one.
With me, large-eyed one, you too worship Adhokshaja, Hrishikesha, intent on fasting, by which you will attain nirvana free of burning or dissolution."
Mohini said: "Well said by you, O king, the worship of the discus-bearer, cutter of birth, death and old age; I shall do so at your command.
The promise you made earlier on Mandara's peak, with giving of the hand, marked by your merit —
the time of that agreement has come; let it be given to me by you. The merit you earned with effort from birth
all of it will quickly perish if you do not give the boon." Rukmangada said: "Come, fair-limbed one, I shall do what is in your mind.
Nothing is ungiveable to you as long as I live; what then of village wealth and land, O lady?"
Mohini said: "Lord, beloved, king, lord of my life, delighter in love! You must not fast on Vishnu's day if I am dear to you; you must eat.
If I am not dear to you, O king, I do not wish it even a moment. Without union with you I will be one without a boon.
Therefore if you wish me, devoted to truth, then give up the fast and eat on Hari's day.
This very boon is to be given, which I asked before; if you do not give, O best of kings, you will become a speaker of untruth,
and go to dreadful hell until the dissolution of beings." The king said: "Do not speak so, auspicious one; this does not suit you.
Being a daughter of the Creator, why do you obstruct dharma? From birth I have never eaten on Hari's day.
How shall I, grey-haired now, eat today, auspicious one? For a mortal past youth, with his strength of senses worn out,
service of the golden river (Ganga) or worship of Hari is proper. What I did not do in childhood or in youth,
how can I, now weak in vigour, do this censured thing? Be gracious, restless-glanced one; be gracious, fair-hued one.
Do not break the vow. I shall give the wealth of kingdoms. Or if you do not wish that, I shall do something else, fair-eyed one:
placing you in a lovely palanquin like an aerial car, I shall take you wherever you wish, walking on foot with my wives.
If you do not wish that either — a vehicle has been made by me — then, having made two golden pillars adorned with coral,
I shall make a swing of pearls for you, dear; I shall swing you there for many months, day and night.
Do not make me break the vow, fair-thighed one, my dear. Better is the flesh of a dog-cooker, or of a dog, fair-faced one,
or even one's own flesh eaten by men, than eating on Hari's day. The sin of killing the three worlds, of intercourse at the waning of the moon,
the sin in a man's shaving on a new-moon-less day, in eating on Vishnu's day, in oil on the sixth,
salt on the third, meat on the seventh, ghee on the full moon, liquor on the sun's transit,
in destroying pasture, false witness, stealing a deposit, obstructing a maiden,
betraying a trusting person, not milking a cow whose calf has died, promising 'I shall give' to a best Brahmin and not giving,
false jewels, false scales, lying about a maiden or a cow — whatever sin there is, is lodged in the food on Hari's day.
Knowing that, lovely-eyed one, how shall I eat that which burns?" Mohini said: "By eating once, eating at night, not asking,
by fasting, O king, one should not transgress the twelfth. For pregnant women, householders, the weak and the ill,
children, those with wrinkled limbs, fasting is not proper; for those set on sacrifice and enjoyment, for those serving a soldier's land,
for devoted wives, O king, fasting is not proper. Gautama told me this when I stood on Mandara.
Vishnu's day is not to be spent without a vow, O best of men. Householders are to be known as those Brahmins who keep a fire;
kings are known as those who engage in protecting subjects. The pregnant one is eight months, children eight years,
those overweight, weak, wrinkled-limbed, the old, those busy with weddings and auspicious rites and festivals,
and those who turned from engagement and are set on sacrifices — by the threefold Purana, the woman devoted to her husband's welfare
is to be known as devoted to her husband, and protector of her womb. What use are other things said in many words, O king?
If you eat on Ekadashi, I am pleased; I am not pleased if you give me your own head cut off.
If, O king, you do not eat on Hari's day, then, as one of untrue speech, I will not touch your body.
Truth is honoured by all classes and orders of life, O king, especially by kings like you, lord of the earth.
By truth the sun burns, by truth the moon shines; the earth rests on truth, O king; truth sustains the world.
By truth the wind blows, by truth fire blazes; this whole world, moving and unmoving, rests on truth."
